title: TELP, a sensitive and versatile library construction method for next-generation sequencing
boundary: TdT poly-C tailing of ssDNA or dsDNA-derived fragments precedes biotin-anchor primed extension, ExoI removal of excess anchor, streptavidin capture, on-bead adapter ligation and PCR. This independent library construction differs from generic double-stranded ligation and single-stranded ancient-DNA capture. Existing fC-CET delegates an opaque adapted TELP continuation and Paired-seq cites its component; neither registers or reconstructs the standalone TELP preparation. DNA/cDNA applications are one method.

title: SALP, a new single-stranded DNA library preparation method especially useful for the high-throughput characterization of chromatin openness states
boundary: Denatured DNA is joined to a partially duplex single-strand adapter with a short degenerate3prime overhang, then copied and amplified. The tagmentation route uses one barcoded Tn5-adapter species followed by SSA installation, instead of requiring a productive pair of different Tn5 adapters; samples can pool after tagged tagmentation. This downstream adaptor/copying boundary differs from ATAC or changing its transposase alone. Fragmentation alternatives,1–4N adapter optimization and cell panels remain one SALP method.

title: Long-adapter single-strand oligonucleotide probes for the massively multiplexed cloning of kilobase genome regions
boundary: Probe libraries assembled from short synthetic oligonucleotide pools incorporate a long adapter scaffold for multiplex capture of kilobase DNA regions, with an actual captured-ORFeome sequencing endpoint in Fig5. This is a probe-construction and long-target capture frontend, not merely a new MIP target panel; full gap-fill/circularization/enrichment chemistry must still be checked locally before collection. Cloning/expression and sequencing outputs must remain distinguished. Later recombinase-based factories or application panels are not extra leads here.
